minify_new_observation.note: NOT tested on preprod's run file for this capability — new finding. minify=true does not just slim the row, it NULLS/ZEROES fields that are populated and correct under the default query. Example: plan 182865 (Testing parikshit) shows test_runs_count:{active:1,closed:0} under the default query (it has one real linked run, TR-5217429) but test_runs_count:{active:0,closed:0} under minify=true — a real, non-zero count silently replaced with zero. Also under minify=true: tags becomes null (declared array, was [] under default), issues becomes null (declared array, was [] under default), test_plan_progress_v2 becomes null (declared object, was a populated rollup under default) on every row including top-level (non-sub-plan) plans. This goes beyond the documented 'slim plan rows' framing — minify=true silently discards true data on a live field (test_runs_count), not just omits optional detail.

notes: PREPROD VERDICT REPRODUCES. Both preprod DRIFT reasons hold on production with real, much larger data (69 real plans vs preprod's 15-item pool, across 3 real pages instead of a forced single page): (1) the same six undeclared fields appear on every row; (2) info.count desyncs from the actual paginated row count once include_sub_plans=true is set — confirmed on a real page mixing 24 top-level + 6 sub-plan rows, where info.count still reports 69 (the top-level-only total). NEW ON PROD (not exercised by preprod's synthetic pool): minify=true silently zeroes/nulls fields that carry real, non-zero data under the default query — most notably test_runs_count, which goes from a correct {active:1,closed:0} to a false {active:0,closed:0} for a plan with a genuinely linked run. This is a materially worse finding than 'minify strips detail' — it makes a real linked-run plan look like it has zero runs. The q filter is unusable through this MCP surface in any shape tried: a nested q object 400s regardless of its sub-key content (query, tags both tried), and bracket-notation query keys (q[query]) are rejected by the MCP tool's own parameter allowlist before any HTTP request is made — so on prod, as on preprod, `q` neither filters nor silently ignores; it hard-fails every reachable shape. Compare to the sibling v2 projects listing on this same account, which silently ignores its filter params instead of erroring — list_test_plans_by_integer_id's failure mode is a harder, more visible failure (400/blocked) rather than a silent no-op, which is arguably the better of two bad options for a caller, but it still means the documented filter surface is not usable as described. Pagination mechanics (p, page_size=30, info envelope) are otherwise clean and internally consistent across 3 real pages: no per_page override exists (not offered in the query schema, none tried) and only p moves the page, matching declared guidance exactly.
